Extract Pointwise Log-Likelihood Draws

Source: R/loo.R
log_lik.Rd

Extract posterior pointwise log-likelihood draws from a fitted brma object. The result is an \(S \times K\) or \(S \times G\) matrix, where \(S\) is the number of posterior draws, \(K\) is the number of estimates, and \(G\) is the number of clusters.

Usage

log_lik(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'brma'
log_lik(object, unit = "estimate", ...)

Arguments

object

a brma model object.

...

currently unused.

unit

output unit. See add_loo.

Value

An \(S \times K\) or \(S \times G\) matrix of pointwise log-likelihood draws with RoBMA_target metadata.

Details

This function returns posterior log-likelihood draws, not a scalar maximized log-likelihood. The logLik.brma method returns the same matrix for the stats::logLik() generic; AIC() and BIC() are not defined for it.

The log-likelihood is computed for each target at each posterior sample. For binomial and Poisson models, each observation consists of a pair of counts (ai/ci or x1i/x2i) that together define a single effect size estimate. Estimate-unit columns condition on the retained observations in each declared dependency block. For Gaussian targets after integrating their declared local Gaussian sources, including correlated known-V brma.mv() and specialized multilevel normal models, these are Schur conditional scores \(p(y_i \mid y_{-i}, \theta)\); their row sum generally is not the full joint likelihood. Likelihood powers and their normalizing constants are retained inside the local-effect integral for weighted Gaussian cluster models. The observation CDF used by residuals remains unpowered. Numerically unresolved retained moments raise RoBMA_weighted_gaussian_unavailable. Likelihood powers and retained-sampling context follow the declared target. Independent observations reduce to ordinary pointwise contributions. Cluster-unit columns delete each complete cluster jointly. Sampling-conditioned selection models retain the declared remaining sampling errors and random context for estimate deletion, including ordinary component branches and constant selection weights. Cluster deletion keeps its distinct joint target. Earlier affected estimate scores must be recomputed. Estimate-unit GLMM draws integrate the nuisance base rate or log-rate over its prior: point priors and untruncated beta (base rate) and normal (log-rate) priors adaptively, other priors on a refined prior-CDF grid; a uniform(0, 1) base-rate prior is a Beta(1, 1) prior and is integrated adaptively. The adaptive Gauss-Hermite rules raise the quadrature order until successive orders agree within the tolerance; this agreement is an empirical refinement check, not an error bound. The grid is accepted only when its log-likelihood changes by less than 1e-6 between refinements. Any nuisance prior without an adaptive route (other than an untruncated beta base rate or an untruncated normal log-rate; truncated ones take the grid too) can fail to reach this, especially with few events or very large arms, and then stops with the error class RoBMA_glmm_grid_nonconvergence described below; gamma, lognormal, and inverse-gamma log-rate priors and lognormal base-rate priors are examples. A beta base-rate prior or a normal log-rate prior avoids it. The automatic computation after fitting (the autocompute.loo and autocompute.waic options) warns instead and returns the fit without LOO/WAIC. Numerical quadrature failures share class RoBMA_glmm_numerical_error. AGHQ failures have class RoBMA_glmm_aghq_nonconvergence; prior-CDF refinement failures retain RoBMA_glmm_grid_nonconvergence. Their fields identify the outcome family, observation, and available sample/refinement diagnostics. A beta baserate prior whose shapes are too extreme for the prior-CDF grid to be represented in double precision is unavailable and raises RoBMA_glmm_prior_unavailable, also of class RoBMA_glmm_numerical_error. Cluster-unit GLMM draws are unavailable until certified nested adaptive quadrature is implemented.

loo.brma, add_waic
